source_meta._title: Burn time indicator of a furnace not working correctly after reloading the world

stor.environment: Unmodified Minecraft Java Edition 1.4.7 client in a single-player world. Use Creative mode as a practical way to obtain the furnace and test items without introducing crafting or resource-gathering delays. Default controls are assumed: E opens the inventory, Esc opens the pause menu or closes an interface, and right-click performs Use Item/Place Block.
preconditions: Configure the Minecraft Launcher to start the exact affected release Minecraft 1.4.7; do not use the fix version 1.21.4 Pre-Release 2.
Use a disposable single-player world because the procedure requires saving, quitting, and reopening the same save.
Use a vanilla client without mods that alter furnaces, inventories, smelting, or furnace interfaces.
No particular world seed, biome, coordinates, difficulty, or server configuration is specified by the report.
The deterministic item choice for this plan is at least 8 Iron Ore as the smelting input, at least 2 Coal as the original long-burning fuel, and at least 1 Stick as the shorter replacement fuel.
Keep the furnace near the player's initial location so the same furnace can be found immediately after the world reload.

steps.action: Start the game using the launcher installation for the exact recommended affected version, Minecraft 1.4.7. Wait for the main menu to finish loading.
steps.exact_input: Minecraft 1.4.7
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft 1.4.7 main menu is displayed and accepts input.

steps.action: Create a new single-player world in Creative mode, or open an existing disposable Creative-mode world. For a new world, choose Singleplayer, create a world, set the game mode to Creative, and enter the world.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player is in a responsive single-player world and can access the Creative inventory.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory with the inventory control, whose default key is E. Obtain and place in the player inventory or hotbar one Furnace, at least eight Iron Ore, at least two Coal, and at least one Stick. Close the inventory when finished.
steps.exact_input: E; obtain Furnace x1, Iron Ore x8 or more, Coal x2 or more, and Stick x1 or more
steps.success_cue: The player inventory contains a furnace, multiple pieces of iron ore, at least two coal, and at least one stick.

steps.action: Select the furnace in the hotbar. Stand near the world's initial player location, aim at the top or side of a solid ground block, and use the Place Block control, whose default input is right-click, to place the furnace.
steps.exact_input: Select Furnace; right-click a solid block face
steps.success_cue: One furnace block is placed nearby and can be reached without exploration after reloading the world.

steps.action: Aim at the placed furnace and use the Use Item control, whose default input is right-click, to open its interface.
steps.exact_input: right-click the placed furnace
steps.success_cue: The furnace interface is open, showing an upper input slot, a lower fuel slot, and an output slot.

steps.action: Move at least eight Iron Ore from the player inventory into the furnace's upper input slot. Use enough input items that the furnace can continue smelting while the following actions are performed.
steps.exact_input: Iron Ore x8 or more -> upper furnace input slot
steps.success_cue: The upper input slot contains iron ore and the fuel slot is still available.

steps.action: Move a stack containing at least two Coal into the lower fuel slot. One coal should be consumed to start the active burn while at least one additional coal remains visible in the fuel slot.
steps.exact_input: Coal x2 or more -> lower furnace fuel slot
steps.success_cue: The furnace is actively burning: the flame symbol is lit, smelting progress has started, and at least one unconsumed coal remains in the lower fuel slot.

steps.action: Keep the furnace interface open and allow the active coal's burn time to decrease. Continue only after the flame-shaped burn-time indicator has visibly shortened from its initial full height while remaining lit. Do not wait for the active coal to finish burning.
steps.success_cue: The flame indicator is still lit but is visibly lower than when the coal was first consumed, and iron ore remains available to smelt.

steps.action: Remove all unconsumed coal from the lower fuel slot without disturbing the iron ore. With the cursor empty, left-click the coal in the fuel slot to pick it up, then left-click an empty player-inventory slot to store it.
steps.exact_input: left-click remaining Coal in fuel slot; left-click an empty player-inventory slot
steps.success_cue: The lower fuel slot is empty, the unused coal has been moved into the player inventory, and the furnace remains in the middle of the burn started by the already-consumed coal.

steps.action: Replace the removed coal with the shorter-burning fuel. Pick up at least one Stick from the player inventory with left-click, then left-click the empty lower fuel slot to place the stick there.
steps.exact_input: left-click Stick; left-click lower furnace fuel slot
steps.success_cue: The lower fuel slot contains a stick while the furnace's already-active coal burn is still in progress.

steps.action: Immediately close the furnace interface using Esc. Do not remain in the world long enough for the current active burn to expire.
steps.exact_input: Esc
steps.success_cue: The world view is visible again, and the same furnace remains nearby.

steps.action: Open the pause menu with Esc and select Save and Quit to Title. This must be done while the furnace is still using the remaining burn time from the consumed coal and a stick is stored in its fuel slot.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Save and Quit to Title
steps.success_cue: The main menu is displayed, confirming that the single-player world was saved and closed.

steps.action: Choose Singleplayer, select the exact same saved world, and load it again. Do not create a replacement world.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> select the same world -> Play Selected World
steps.success_cue: The player has re-entered the same save containing the prepared furnace.

steps.action: Wait until the local terrain and the furnace have rendered and player movement responds normally. Locate the nearby furnace placed before quitting.
steps.success_cue: The prepared furnace is visible, the surrounding chunk is loaded, and normal movement and interaction are responsive.

steps.action: Aim at the same furnace and right-click it once to open its interface. Do not remove, insert, or rearrange any items after opening it; hand control to the observation subsystem immediately.
steps.exact_input: right-click the prepared furnace
steps.success_cue: The reloaded furnace interface is open with its saved inventory available for inspection, and no post-reload item interaction has occurred.

stor.handoff_condition: The same prepared furnace has just been opened after saving, quitting, and reloading the world. The furnace interface is visible, and the player has not changed any furnace contents since reopening it. Begin observation of the burn-time indicator now.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode. Creative mode is selected only as a practical, deterministic method of obtaining the required materials; it is not asserted to be a required bug condition.

The report does not specify a smelting input or an exact long-fuel/short-fuel pair. Iron Ore, Coal, and Stick are chosen as a deterministic implementation of its requirements: start with a non-stick fuel, then replace the unconsumed fuel-slot contents with a shorter-burning fuel.

The report gives no exact duration for allowing the first burn to decrease. This plan therefore uses the report's observable condition—the flame indicator must visibly shorten while remaining active—instead of imposing an unsupported fixed delay.

A comment says that unloading and reloading the furnace's chunk can also trigger the issue without manually swapping fuel. This plan deliberately follows the primary description's Save and Quit procedure and explicit fuel swap rather than substituting the alternate chunk-unloading reproduction.
No seed or coordinates are supplied. Placing the furnace close to the initial player location is an execution convenience, not a reported requirement.

source_meta._title: Damage wobble no longer shows direction of incoming damage

stor.environment: Unmodified Minecraft: Java Edition 1.5.2 in a new single-player world. Build the apparatus in Creative mode, then enable commands through Open to LAN and enter Survival mode before taking damage. The single-player integrated server preserves the post-1.3 client/server condition relevant to the report. Use first-person view and a flat, unobstructed outdoor area.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact Java Edition 1.5.2 release, not the similarly numbered pre-release, a later affected version, or the fixed version 23w03a.
Use a vanilla client without mods that alter the camera, damage animation, player invulnerability, dispensers, projectiles, or networking.
Use first-person view. Press F5 as needed until the player's body is not visible in front of the camera.
Know the bindings for Move Forward, Move Back, Strafe Left, and Strafe Right; their default inputs are W, S, A, and D.
The trigger must occur in Survival mode with the player at full or nearly full health. Creative-mode arrow launches may be used only to validate the apparatus.

The report's attachment showing the original contraption is not included in the supplied data. The steps therefore construct a minimal four-direction cross that implements the report's stated dispenser, arrow, and pressure-plate relationships.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation using release 1.5.2 and start it. Do not select the 1.5.2 pre-release or the fixed snapshot 23w03a.
steps.exact_input: Release 1.5.2
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is open and the displayed game version is 1.5.2.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, select Create New World, give the world an identifiable name, set Game Mode to Creative, and create the world. A seed is not specified, so any seed may be used.
steps.exact_input: World name: MC-26678 reproduction; Game Mode: Creative
steps.success_cue: A new world has loaded and the player is in Creative mode, indicated by the absence of Survival hearts and hunger and by the ability to fly after double-tapping Space.

steps.action: Wait before building. Do not continue until nearby terrain has rendered and walking, looking, inventory opening, and block placement respond normally.
steps.success_cue: The surrounding terrain is visible and player controls respond without chunk-loading pauses.

steps.action: Locate or make a flat, unobstructed area at least 9 blocks by 9 blocks. Remove tall grass, snow layers, water, walls, mobs, or other objects that could obstruct an arrow fired horizontally at the player.
steps.exact_input: left-click to remove obstructing blocks
steps.success_cue: A flat 9-by-9 test area is available with clear horizontal space around its center.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Obtain four Dispensers, four Stone Pressure Plates, at least 64 Arrows, and several visually distinctive marker blocks such as colored wool. Put the dispensers, pressure plates, arrows, and marker blocks into accessible hotbar or inventory slots, then close the inventory.
steps.exact_input: E; Creative inventory items: Dispenser, Stone Pressure Plate, Arrow, and a distinctive marker block
steps.success_cue: The player has four dispensers, four stone pressure plates, at least 64 arrows, and marker blocks available.

steps.action: Choose one ground block near the middle of the cleared area as the central standing position, referred to as C. Place a distinctive marker block beside C without occupying C itself.
steps.exact_input: right-click with the marker block selected
steps.success_cue: The central standing block C is visually identifiable and remains empty so the player can stand on it.

steps.action: Stand on C and choose an arbitrary horizontal direction as 'forward.' Four blocks forward from C, build a marker pillar at least three blocks tall. This pillar defines the fixed facing direction for every test and should remain visible above the apparatus.
steps.exact_input: W to move forward; right-click to place marker blocks
steps.success_cue: A tall forward marker is four blocks from C, and it can be seen from C when the player faces forward.

steps.action: Build the front launcher. The front dispenser belongs two blocks forward from C, between C and the marker pillar. Stand on the block one step forward from C, face away from C toward the intended dispenser position, select a dispenser, and place it on the ground two blocks forward from C. Confirm that the dispenser's opening faces back toward C; break and replace it if its opening points elsewhere.
steps.exact_input: Select Dispenser; right-click to place
steps.success_cue: A dispenser is two blocks forward from C and its firing opening points toward C.

steps.action: Place a stone pressure plate on the ground one block forward from C, directly between C and the front dispenser. The plate must be horizontally adjacent to the dispenser's firing face.
steps.exact_input: Select Stone Pressure Plate; right-click to place
steps.success_cue: The front row, viewed from C, is C -> front pressure plate -> inward-facing front dispenser.

steps.action: Return to C and face the forward marker. Build the right launcher two blocks directly to the player's right. Stand on the future right-pressure-plate position, face outward away from C, and place the dispenser. Confirm that its opening faces inward toward C.
steps.exact_input: D to move right; select Dispenser; right-click to place
steps.success_cue: A dispenser is two blocks to the right of C, relative to the forward marker, and its opening points toward C.

steps.action: Place a stone pressure plate one block directly to the right of C, between C and the right dispenser. Keep the plate immediately adjacent to the dispenser's firing face.
steps.exact_input: Select Stone Pressure Plate; right-click to place
steps.success_cue: The right row is C -> right pressure plate -> inward-facing right dispenser.

steps.action: Return to C and face the forward marker. Build the rear launcher two blocks directly behind the player. Stand on the future rear-pressure-plate position, face outward away from C, and place the dispenser. Confirm that its opening faces inward toward C.
steps.exact_input: S to move backward; select Dispenser; right-click to place
steps.success_cue: A dispenser is two blocks behind C and its opening points toward C.

steps.action: Place a stone pressure plate one block directly behind C, between C and the rear dispenser.
steps.exact_input: Select Stone Pressure Plate; right-click to place
steps.success_cue: The rear row is C -> rear pressure plate -> inward-facing rear dispenser.

steps.action: Return to C and face the forward marker. Build the left launcher two blocks directly to the player's left. Stand on the future left-pressure-plate position, face outward away from C, and place the dispenser. Confirm that its opening faces inward toward C.
steps.exact_input: A to move left; select Dispenser; right-click to place
steps.success_cue: A dispenser is two blocks to the left of C and its opening points toward C.

steps.action: Place a stone pressure plate one block directly to the left of C, between C and the left dispenser. Inspect the completed apparatus from above or while flying: it should form a cross with C in the middle, one pressure plate on each side of C, and one inward-facing dispenser immediately beyond each plate.
steps.exact_input: Select Stone Pressure Plate; right-click to place
steps.success_cue: The completed top-down arrangement is front dispenser/plate, left dispenser/plate, C, right plate/dispenser, and rear plate/dispenser, with all four dispenser openings aimed toward C.

steps.action: Load the dispensers. Right-click each of the four dispensers to open its nine-slot interface, move at least 16 arrows into any slot, and close the interface. Repeat until every dispenser contains arrows.
steps.exact_input: right-click each Dispenser; transfer at least 16 Arrows into each
steps.success_cue: Each of the four dispensers contains arrows and can fire multiple times.

steps.action: While still in Creative mode, validate the right-side mechanism without evaluating camera behavior. Stand on C, face the forward marker, and move right with D until the right pressure plate depresses. An immediately adjacent pressure plate can activate the dispenser without extra wiring. Return to C after one launch and do not rotate the camera. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3ADefense?utm_source=openai))
steps.exact_input: D, then A to return to C
steps.success_cue: The right pressure plate clicks down and the right dispenser produces one launch sound or visible arrow; the dispenser still contains additional arrows.

steps.action: Enable commands for the current single-player session. Press Esc, select Open to LAN, set Allow Cheats to ON, and select Start LAN World. Leave the game mode option otherwise unchanged; the host player's mode will be changed with a command in the next step.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Open to LAN -> Allow Cheats: ON -> Start LAN World
steps.success_cue: The world resumes and chat reports that the local game has been hosted, confirming that the LAN session started.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat. Type the exact historical command `/gamemode 0`, including the leading slash, and press Enter. Numeric game-mode values and the `gamemode <mode> [player]` argument order are appropriate for this pre-1.13 version. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Minecraft_Wiki%3AIssues/Weekly_12w16a?utm_source=openai))
steps.exact_input: /gamemode 0
steps.success_cue: The command succeeds, Survival hearts and hunger appear, and the player is no longer invulnerable or able to fly.

steps.action: Prepare the directional trigger. Stand exactly on C, allow any Creative-flight state to end, and wait until the player is stationary. Ensure sufficient health to survive one dispenser arrow. Face the tall forward marker so the right dispenser is exactly on the player's right; do not rotate the camera after establishing this orientation.
steps.exact_input: Move onto C; align view with the forward marker
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary on C in Survival mode, facing the forward marker, with the loaded right dispenser two blocks to the player's right.

steps.action: Without turning the camera, hold the Strafe Right action, default key D, just long enough to step from C onto the right pressure plate. Release D as soon as the plate activates. Do not move or rotate after the arrow hits.
steps.exact_input: D
steps.success_cue: The right pressure plate depresses, the right dispenser fires from the player's right, and the Survival player takes one arrow hit while still facing the forward marker.

stor.handoff_condition: The Survival player has just been struck once by an arrow fired from the dispenser on the player's right while the player remains oriented toward the forward marker. Begin observing the immediate viewport/camera damage response before the player moves, turns, or receives another hit.
uncertainties: The original image attachment, `2014-10-30_22.38.46.png`, is referenced but not present in the supplied report, and its exact block layout could not be retrieved. The four-way cross is a minimal reconstruction based on the report's explicit left, right, front, and rear pressure-plate instructions rather than a claim that every block matches the attachment.

The report asks for all four directional movements. This plan constructs and loads all four launchers but uses the right-side strike as the single deterministic handoff trigger. After that capture, the same setup can support separate left, front, and rear trials by returning to C, restoring health if necessary, facing the same marker, and using A, W, or S respectively.

No world seed, coordinates, difficulty, pressure-plate material, or exact arrow quantity is specified. The flat location, stone pressure plates, and minimum arrow counts are practical execution choices and are not asserted as required causes of the issue.

If a dispenser fails the Creative-mode validation, the most likely setup error is its facing direction or separation from the pressure plate. Rebuild it so its opening points toward C and its firing face is directly adjacent to the plate before entering Survival.
Historical Minecraft 1.5.2 may require a compatible Java runtime and launcher configuration; those platform-specific installation details are outside the Mojira reproduction information.

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition in singleplayer, using the integrated server and the prepared world attachment named "Minecraft bug MC-4 testcase for debug.zip". Launch the exact first-listed affected version, "Minecraft 1.4.1". Retain the world state supplied by the attachment; do not change its game mode, blocks, entities, player location, or other settings before the trigger.
preconditions: The launcher must have an installation that runs the exact report-listed version "Minecraft 1.4.1"; do not substitute Minecraft 1.4.2 or a fix version.
Obtain the exact MC-4 attachment "Minecraft bug MC-4 testcase for debug.zip". This is the edited test world identified in the report comments as a consistent and easy reproduction case.
Keep an untouched backup of the ZIP archive and the extracted world so that every attempt can start from the original saved state.

Install the extracted world in the saves directory used by the Minecraft 1.4.1 launcher installation. The final world folder must contain level.dat directly inside it, rather than level.dat being hidden inside an extra nested folder.
Do not open or convert the test world in a newer Minecraft version before this attempt.
The observation or screen-capture subsystem must be ready before the world is opened because loading the prepared world is the trigger action.
No command permissions or command-block construction are required for this selected reproduction route; the supplied debug world replaces the report's later, version-incompatible command-based setup.

steps.action: Obtain the prepared debug-world attachment from MC-4 and preserve it without editing its contents.
steps.exact_input: Minecraft bug MC-4 testcase for debug.zip
steps.success_cue: The exact ZIP archive is available locally and a separate untouched copy has been retained for resetting the test.

steps.action: Locate the game directory assigned to the Minecraft 1.4.1 launcher installation, open its saves directory, and extract the debug-world ZIP there. If the ZIP produces an outer wrapper directory, move the actual world directory into saves so that the world directory itself directly contains level.dat.
steps.exact_input: Minecraft bug MC-4 testcase for debug.zip
steps.success_cue: One newly imported world folder is present under the selected installation's saves directory, and level.dat is directly inside that folder.

steps.action: Start the Minecraft Launcher, select the installation configured for the exact report-listed version "Minecraft 1.4.1", and launch the game. Do not use Minecraft 1.8.1-pre1 or another version merely because it appears in the Fix versions field.
steps.exact_input: Minecraft 1.4.1
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is open and the displayed version identifies the running client as Minecraft 1.4.1.

steps.action: From the main menu, select Singleplayer and wait for the saved-world list to finish loading.
steps.success_cue: The Select World screen is open and the imported world appears in the list.

steps.action: Identify the newly imported world associated with "Minecraft bug MC-4 testcase for debug.zip". Select it once, but do not open it yet. If other worlds are present and the display name is not the archive filename, identify it by the fact that it was the world newly added during step 2.
steps.exact_input: Minecraft bug MC-4 testcase for debug.zip
steps.success_cue: The imported MC-4 debug world is highlighted in the world list, while the player is still on the Select World screen.

steps.action: Confirm that the observation or screen-capture subsystem is active and ready to inspect the first moments after loading. Do not enter another world first, because the supplied report states that reopening this prepared world resets its test sequence.
steps.success_cue: Observation is active, the MC-4 debug world remains highlighted, and no world-loading action has occurred yet.

steps.action: Open the selected debug world by clicking Play Selected World or by double-clicking its highlighted list entry. Do not press movement, attack, use, drop, inventory, or menu controls during the initial load.
steps.success_cue: The world-loading screen appears or the prepared world begins rendering; no post-load player input has been issued.

stor.handoff_condition: The original, unmodified MC-4 debug world has just been opened in Minecraft 1.4.1. Hand control to the observation subsystem immediately and observe continuously from the loading transition through initial terrain and entity rendering without issuing player input.
uncertainties: The current formal reproduction command in the report, "teleport @e[type=item,distance=..6] ~ ~1 ~-0.6249", cannot be executed unchanged in the recommended first affected version. The /teleport command was added in Java Edition 1.10 Pre-Release 1, and the selector argument name distance belongs to the command rewrite associated with Java Edition 1.13. ([zh.minecraft.wiki](https://zh.minecraft.wiki/w/%E5%91%BD%E4%BB%A4/teleport?utm_source=openai)) The plan therefore uses the attached debug world that report comments identify as the easiest consistent test case.

The attachment's internal world-folder name, in-game display name, player coordinates, facing direction, and exact block layout are not supplied in the text of the report. The executor must identify the newly imported world by installation time rather than by an assumed display name.

The attachment bytes are not included in the raw report provided to this agent. Reproduction depends on successfully obtaining the exact attachment "Minecraft bug MC-4 testcase for debug.zip" from MC-4.
The report does not specify a game mode for the debug world. Preserve the mode stored in the attachment rather than selecting or changing one.

The report's formal command-based procedure could be used on an affected version with compatible command syntax, but doing so would conflict with the required selection of the first listed affected version. No unverified historical rewrite of that command has been invented.

source_meta._title: Client continues to connect to server after canceling on 'Connecting to server' screen

stor.environment: A clean, unmodified Minecraft Java Edition 1.8 client using one authenticated account, plus two distinct multiplayer servers designated Server A and Server B. Both servers must accept 1.8 clients and the account must be permitted to join both. Server A must be reachable but its connection must remain on the client’s "Connecting to server" screen long enough to press Cancel; a delayed DNS lookup, proxy, network shaper, or naturally slow connection may be used to create that window. Server B should be normally reachable. Keep both server entries prepared in the Multiplayer server list so Server B can be selected immediately after canceling Server A. Use a newly started client process and do not restart Minecraft between the two connection attempts.
preconditions: Install or select the exact affected release Minecraft 1.8; do not use the fixed version 1.20 Pre-release 5.
Use a vanilla client without client mods, because the report was confirmed on vanilla.
Obtain the addresses of two different servers, Server A and Server B, that are compatible with Minecraft 1.8 and can be joined by the same account.

Configure Server A or its network path so that selecting it leaves the client on the "Connecting to server" screen for long enough to click Cancel, while still allowing the connection attempt to continue toward a real, reachable server.
Ensure Server B is online and normally reachable before beginning the timed portion of the reproduction.
Fully close any previous Minecraft client process before the attempt, then launch a fresh client to avoid carrying over state from an earlier attempt.
Do not disconnect normally from Server A, restart the client, or intentionally pause between canceling Server A and starting the connection to Server B.
The timing is important: if Server A displays its world before Cancel is clicked, that attempt is invalid and must be repeated with a longer connection delay.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select an installation configured for the exact release Minecraft 1.8 and start the game.
steps.exact_input: Minecraft 1.8
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft title screen is open and identifies the running game version as Minecraft 1.8.

steps.action: From the title screen, left-click Multiplayer to open the multiplayer server list.
steps.exact_input: Multiplayer
steps.success_cue: The Play Multiplayer screen is visible and no world or server is currently open.

steps.action: If Server A is not already listed, left-click Add Server, enter a recognizable name and the delayed Server A address supplied by the test environment, and then left-click Done.
steps.exact_input: Server Name: Server A; Server Address: <delayed Server A address>
steps.success_cue: A row named Server A is visible in the multiplayer server list.

steps.action: If Server B is not already listed, left-click Add Server, enter a recognizable name and the Server B address supplied by the test environment, and then left-click Done.
steps.exact_input: Server Name: Server B; Server Address: <Server B address>
steps.success_cue: Separate rows named Server A and Server B are visible in the multiplayer server list.

steps.action: Allow the server list to update only long enough to confirm that Server B is online. Do not begin the timed connection sequence until Server A's delay mechanism is active.
steps.success_cue: Server B is available for joining, Server A's delayed connection path is active, and both rows remain visible.

steps.action: Left-click the Server A row once so that Server A is the selected server.
steps.exact_input: Server A
steps.success_cue: Server A is highlighted in the server list and Server B is not selected.

steps.action: Start joining Server A by left-clicking Join Server or by double-clicking the Server A row.
steps.exact_input: Join Server
steps.success_cue: The server list is replaced by a connection-status screen.

steps.action: Wait only until the status screen visibly says "Connecting to server" and its Cancel button is available. Do not wait for terrain, a loading world, or Server A's in-game view. If Server A's world appears before this state can be acted on, disconnect normally, return to the server list, increase Server A's connection delay, and restart the attempt from a fresh client process.
steps.exact_input: Connecting to server
steps.success_cue: The client is still on the "Connecting to server" screen, the Cancel button is clickable, and Server A's world has not appeared.

steps.action: While the screen still says "Connecting to server", immediately left-click Cancel once.
steps.exact_input: Cancel
steps.success_cue: The connection-status screen closes without ever displaying Server A's world, and the client returns to either the multiplayer server list or the title screen.

steps.action: If Cancel returned the client to the title screen, immediately left-click Multiplayer. If the multiplayer server list is already visible, perform no extra navigation. Do not restart or close the game.
steps.exact_input: Multiplayer
steps.success_cue: The multiplayer server list containing Server A and Server B is visible in the same client process used for the canceled connection.

steps.action: Without an intentional delay, left-click the Server B row once.
steps.exact_input: Server B
steps.success_cue: Server B is highlighted in the server list.

steps.action: Immediately start joining Server B by left-clicking Join Server or by double-clicking the Server B row.
steps.exact_input: Join Server
steps.success_cue: The client leaves the server list and begins the connection to Server B without Minecraft having been restarted.

steps.action: Wait for Server B's world to finish loading. Continue only after terrain is rendered, the in-game HUD is visible, and ordinary movement input responds. Do not disconnect, restart, or join another world before handing control to the observation subsystem.
steps.success_cue: The player is in Server B's loaded world in the same client process, immediately following the canceled Server A attempt, and normal in-game input can be issued.

stor.handoff_condition: The client has just completed entry into Server B in the same Minecraft 1.8 process used to press Cancel on Server A's "Connecting to server" screen. Server A was canceled before its world appeared, Server B was joined immediately afterward, and no client restart or normal Server A disconnect occurred. Begin observing the client's connection and world state now.
uncertainties: The report supplies no server addresses, so the executor must provide two distinct Minecraft 1.8-compatible servers.
